other courses recognized by the Director as equivalent; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: that equivalent content has been covered in the bachelor degree programme taken by the applicant.

section.name: s25
section.heading: Appointment of registered fire engineers
section.content: A person may, for making a specified application in relation to any scheduled premises, appoint a registered fire engineer to carry out a duty specified in section 27, 28 or 29 in relation to the premises.

section.name: s26
section.heading: Restrictions on carrying out of duties

subsection.content: A registered fire engineer must not carry out a duty that is not within the scope of duties of the class for which the engineer is registered.
A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 6 and to imprisonment for 1 year.

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer (risk assessment) may carry out the following duties in relation to any scheduled premises—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: to conduct an inspection of, and carry out a fire safety risk assessment for, the scheduled premises for the specified application to which the premises relate;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: to recommend, from a fire safety point of view, to the person who has appointed the registered fire engineer for the inspection and assessment of the suitability of the scheduled premises to be used for the person’s intended purpose;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: subject to subsection (2), to issue for the scheduled premises any requirement relating to fire safety.

subsection.content: Before issuing any fire safety requirement under subsection (1)(c), the registered fire engineer must submit the requirement to the Director for endorsement.
If any fire safety requirement is issued without the Director’s endorsement, the requirement is not valid for any specified application.

subsection.leadIn: The Director may refuse to endorse any fire safety requirement submitted for endorsement under subsection (2) if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the Director is satisfied that, by issuing, or attempting to issue, the requirement, the registered fire engineer has contravened, or is likely to contravene, this Regulation or a code of practice;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the fire safety risk assessment referred to in the requirement was carried out more than 30 days before the date on which the requirement was submitted to the Director for endorsement;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: information required to be given in the specified form for the requirement has not yet been given; or

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: the Director considers that it is inappropriate to endorse the requirement.

subsection.content: The endorsement by the Director of any fire safety requirement under this section does not affect the exercise of any power, or the discharge of any duties, by the Director under the Ordinance.

subsection.leadIn: For the purposes of subsection (1)(a)—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: an inspection is conducted by a registered fire engineer (risk assessment) only if the inspection is personally conducted by the engineer or another person who is under the direct and proper supervision of the engineer at the place at which the inspection takes place; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: an assessment is carried out by a registered fire engineer (risk assessment) only if the assessment is personally carried out by the engineer or another person who is under the direct and proper supervision of the engineer at the place at which the assessment takes place.

subsection.content: For the purposes of subsection (1)(b), a registered fire engineer (risk assessment) may make a recommendation only if the inspection and assessment are personally conducted and carried out by the engineer or another person who is under the direct and proper supervision of the engineer at the place at which the inspection and assessment take place.

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer (fire service installation) may carry out the following duties in relation to any scheduled premises—

subparagraph.content: an inspection of the scheduled premises to verify the premises’ compliance with the fire safety requirement (other than that relating to the ventilating system of the premises); and

a testing of any fire service installation or equipment (other than that relating to the ventilating system of the premises) installed in the scheduled premises to verify the premises’ compliance with the fire safety requirement (other than that relating to the ventilating system of the premises);

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: to issue a fire safety (fire service installation) certificate in the specified form for the scheduled premises if all relevant fire safety requirements (other than those relating to the ventilating system of the premises) are complied with.

subsection.leadIn: The Director may, for the purposes of this Regulation, enter any scheduled premises to carry out an audit check for any fire safety (fire service installation) certificate issued under subsection (1)(b) for the premises—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: during reasonable hours; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: at any other time with the consent of the occupier of the premises.

subsection.content: For the purposes of subsection (1)(a), an inspection and testing are conducted by a registered fire engineer (fire service installation) only if the inspection and testing are personally conducted by the engineer or another person who is under the direct and proper supervision of the engineer at the place at which the inspection and testing take place.

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer (ventilating system) may carry out the following duties in relation to any scheduled premises—

subparagraph.content: an inspection of the scheduled premises to verify the premises’ compliance with the fire safety requirement relating to the ventilating system of the premises; and
a testing of the ventilating system installed in the scheduled premises to verify the premises’ compliance with the fire safety requirement relating to the ventilating system of the premises;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: to issue a fire safety (ventilating system) certificate in the specified form for the scheduled premises if all relevant fire safety requirements relating to the ventilating system of the premises are complied with.

subsection.leadIn: The Director may, for the purposes of this Regulation, enter any scheduled premises to carry out an audit check of any fire safety (ventilating system) certificate issued under subsection (1)(b) for the premises—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: during reasonable hours; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: at any other time with the consent of the occupier of the premises.

subsection.content: For the purposes of subsection (1)(a), an inspection and testing are conducted by a registered fire engineer (ventilating system) only if the inspection and testing are personally conducted by the engineer or another person who is under the direct and proper supervision of the engineer at the place at which the inspection and testing take place.

section.name: s30
section.heading: Duty of registered fire engineer to keep certain documents

subsection.content: A registered fire engineer must keep, for the period specified in subsection (2), a copy of every fire safety requirement and every fire safety certificate (as appropriate), issued by the engineer.

subsection.leadIn: The following period is specified for the purposes of subsection (1)—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: in relation to copies kept for a fire safety requirement—the 3-year period beginning on the date of the issue of the requirement;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: in relation to copies kept for a fire safety certificate—the 3-year period beginning on the date of the issue of the certificate.

subsection.content: If an authorized officer requests a registered fire engineer to produce for the officer’s inspection a copy of any document mentioned in subsection (1), the engineer must comply with the request within 5 days after the date of the receipt of the request.
A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 3 and to imprisonment of 6 months.
A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes subsection (3) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 3.

section.name: s31
section.heading: Duty to notify Director of change in personal particulars

subsection.leadIn: If there is a change in any of the following personal particulars of a registered fire engineer—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: name;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: phone number;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: correspondence address;

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: electronic mail address;

paragraph.name: e
paragraph.content: identity document,

subsection.continued: the engineer must, within 14 days after the date on which the change takes place, notify the Director of the change in the specified form.

subsection.content: A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 1.

section.name: s32
section.heading: Registered fire engineers to carry with them registration cards or produce the cards if required for inspection

subsection.leadIn: This section applies to a registered fire engineer who—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: personally carries out any duties under section 27, 28 or 29; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: supervises another person to carry out such duties.

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer must, at all times while the engineer is at the place at which the duties are carried out, carry—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: if the engineer’s registration card is in electronic form—an electronic device on which the registration card that is relevant to the duties being carried out (relevant registration card) can be readily displayed; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: if the engineer’s registration card is in hard copy form—the registration card.

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer at the place mentioned in subsection (2) must, on being required by an authorized officer, produce—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: if the engineer’s registration card is in electronic form—the relevant registration card for inspection; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: if the engineer’s registration card is in hard copy form—the registration card for inspection.

subsection.content: A person who, without reasonable excuse, fails to comply with subsection (2) or (3) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 1.

division.name: D3
division.heading: Issue of Fire Safety Certificates and Fire Safety Requirements

subsection.leadIn: This section applies in relation to a registered fire engineer (fire service installation) or registered fire engineer (ventilating system) who—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: has conducted an inspection and testing in relation to certain scheduled premises under section 28(1)(a) or 29(1)(a); and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: is satisfied with the result of the inspection and testing.

subsection.leadIn: The registered fire engineer must, within 5 days after completing the inspection and testing—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.leadIn: issue a fire safety certificate to—

subparagraph.content: the person who has appointed the registered fire engineer for the inspection and testing; or
the person’s representative; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: send a copy of the certificate to the Director.

section.name: s34
section.heading: Fire safety requirements and fire safety certificates must be in specified form and signed by registered fire engineer
section.leadIn: Any fire safety requirement or fire safety certificate issued under section 27, 28 or 29 for any scheduled premises—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must be in the specified form; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: must be signed by the registered fire engineer who, in relation to the premises, has—

subparagraph.content: conducted the relevant inspection and carried out the relevant assessment; or
conducted the relevant inspection and testing.

section.name: s35
section.heading: Offences relating to issue of fire safety requirements or fire safety certificates

subsection.leadIn: A registered fire engineer must not—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: issue any fire safety requirement without the Director’s endorsement;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: issue a fire safety certificate that is false or misleading; or

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: issue a fire safety certificate while knowing that the relevant fire safety requirement has not been endorsed by the Director.

subsection.content: A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of $200,000 and to imprisonment for 1 year.

subsection.leadIn: This section applies if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.leadIn: a fire services member has reasonable grounds to suspect that a person (relevant person)—

subparagraph.content: has committed, or is committing, an offence under this Regulation; or
has committed, or is committing, a disciplinary offence; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: the member has reasonable grounds to believe that obtaining the particulars of the relevant person is necessary for—

subparagraph.content: carrying out the member’s duties under this Regulation;
the effective enforcement of this Regulation; or
ascertaining whether a code of practice has been, or is being, complied with.

subsection.leadIn: A fire services member may require the relevant person to—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: provide the person’s name and address; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: produce the person’s identity document.

subsection.content: When exercising the power under subsection (2), a fire services member must, if so requested by a person affected by the exercise, produce for inspection by the person the member’s warrant card issued by the Director as proof of the member’s appointment as a fire services member.

subsection.leadIn: A relevant person who—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: without reasonable excuse, fails to comply with a requirement made under subsection (2); or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: produces any particulars that the person knows to be false in a material particular in connection with a requirement made under subsection (2),

subsection.continued: commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 4.

section.name: s37
section.heading: Disciplinary offences
section.leadIn: A registered fire engineer commits a disciplinary offence if the registered fire engineer—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: commits misconduct or neglect as a registered fire engineer in any professional respect;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: contravenes any condition of the engineer’s registration imposed or amended under section 9(5) or 11(7);

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: has issued a fire safety certificate for compliance with the fire safety requirement of any scheduled premises deviating from the requirement;

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: has failed to discharge the duties, or abide by the requirements, imposed on a registered fire engineer under this Regulation;

paragraph.name: e
paragraph.content: has held himself or herself out to be a registered fire engineer for a class for which he or she is not registered;

paragraph.name: f
paragraph.content: has been convicted of an offence under this Regulation; or

paragraph.name: g
paragraph.content: has been convicted in Hong Kong or elsewhere of any other offence that may bring the profession of registered fire engineer into disrepute.

subsection.content: Despite section 37, a person who discloses the matters specified in subsection (2) to the Director when applying for registration or renewal of registration as a registered fire engineer does not commit any disciplinary offence for those matters if the Director approves the application.

subsection.leadIn: The following matters are specified for the purposes of subsection (1)—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the person has committed misconduct or neglect as a registered fire engineer in a professional respect;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the person has been convicted of an offence under this Regulation;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the person has been convicted in Hong Kong or elsewhere of any other offence that may bring the profession of registered fire engineers into disrepute.

subsection.content: A person may make to the Secretary a complaint of a disciplinary offence against a registered fire engineer.

subsection.leadIn: The complaint is—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: if the complainant is the Director—to be made by the Director to the Secretary directly; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: if the complainant is a person other than the Director—to be referred to the Secretary through the Director in accordance with subsections (3), (4) and (5).

subsection.content: Subject to subsection (5), the Director must refer the complaint to the Secretary within 30 days after the date on which the Director receives the complaint from the complainant.
The Director may refuse to refer the complaint to the Secretary but only on one or more of the grounds specified in section 40.
If the Director refuses to refer the complaint to the Secretary, the Director must, notify the complainant in writing of the fact and the reasons for the refusal.

subsection.leadIn: A complaint under this section—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must be made in the specified form; and

subparagraph.content: details of the complaint; and
the name, address and telephone number of the complainant.

section.name: s40
section.heading: Grounds for refusing to refer complaints to Secretary
section.leadIn: The following grounds are specified for the purposes of section 39(4)—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the complaint is made anonymously;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the complainant cannot be identified or traced;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the complainant fails to provide any information or particulars the Director reasonably requires for processing in relation to the complaint;

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: the person being complained of has ceased to be a registered fire engineer at the time the complaint is made;

paragraph.name: e
paragraph.content: the Director has previously refused to refer the complaint to the Secretary under section 39 and there is no material change in circumstances;

paragraph.name: f
paragraph.content: the complaint, or a complaint of a substantially similar nature, has previously been disposed of by a disciplinary board;

paragraph.name: g
paragraph.leadIn: having regard to all circumstances of the case, the Director is satisfied—

subparagraph.content: that on its face no case has been shown for the complaint;
that the complaint is frivolous or vexatious or not made in good faith;

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: the complaint was made 2 years or more after the alleged disciplinary offence came to the knowledge of the complainant; and

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: there are no special circumstances that explain the delay in making the complaint; or
that referring the complaint to the Secretary is unnecessary for any other reason.

section.name: s41
section.heading: Appointment of disciplinary board
section.content: If a complaint is made or referred to the Secretary under section 39, the Secretary must, within 21 days after receiving the complaint, appoint a board to hear and consider the complaint.

def.name: Party
def.leadIn: party (當事人), in relation to a complaint made under section 39(1), means—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the Director; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the registered fire engineer who is the subject of the complaint.

subsection.leadIn: For hearing a complaint by a disciplinary board, the chairperson of the board is to—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: appoint the time and place of the hearing; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: notify the parties in writing of that time and place.

subsection.leadIn: A party to the hearing may—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: make a representation in person at the hearing; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: be represented at the hearing by a solicitor or counsel, or any other person authorized by the party in writing.

subsection.content: A party to the hearing and the party’s representative (if any) may adduce evidence at any proceedings before the disciplinary board.

section.name: s44
section.heading: Giving of evidence and related offence

subsection.leadIn: For hearing a complaint, the disciplinary board may—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: receive evidence on oath; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: by notice signed by the chairperson of the board, order any person—

subparagraph.content: to attend before the board and to give evidence; or
to produce any document or information relevant to the complaint.

subsection.content: A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes an order made under subsection (1)(b) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 5.

section.name: s45
section.heading: Records of previous conviction of disciplinary offence

subsection.leadIn: This section applies if a registered fire engineer—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: is the subject of a complaint; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: was previously found guilty of a disciplinary offence (previous offence).

subsection.content: Subject to subsection (3), the disciplinary board appointed for the complaint must not inquire into the question whether the registered fire engineer was properly convicted of the previous offence.

If, after hearing the complaint, the disciplinary board convicts the registered fire engineer of a disciplinary offence, the board may, for considering what order to make under section 48, consider any record of the previous offence and any other evidence that may be available and is relevant as showing the nature and gravity of the previous offence.

If a registered fire engineer is alleged to have committed a disciplinary offence at a time when a code of practice was in force, subsection (2) has effect with respect to the code in relation to the alleged offence.

The disciplinary board may, in any proceedings under this Regulation to decide whether a registered fire engineer has committed a disciplinary offence, have regard to any provision of the code that appears to the board to be relevant to the act or omission constituting the offence.

section.name: s47
section.heading: Legal adviser to disciplinary board
section.content: The chairperson of a disciplinary board may appoint a solicitor or counsel as a legal adviser to advise on any legal matters relating to the proceedings of the board.

section.name: s48
section.heading: Orders by disciplinary board after hearing

subsection.content: After hearing a complaint, the disciplinary board may make an order under subsection (2) or (3).

If the disciplinary board decides that the registered fire engineer concerned has not committed the disciplinary offence alleged in the complaint, the board may order that the registered fire engineer be exonerated.

subsection.leadIn: If the disciplinary board decides that the registered fire engineer concerned has committed the disciplinary offence alleged in the complaint, the board may make one or more of the following orders—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: an order that the registered fire engineer be reprimanded;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: an order that the name of the registered fire engineer be removed from the register—

subparagraph.content: permanently; or
temporarily for a period the board considers appropriate.

subsection.leadIn: If the disciplinary board makes an order under this section, the board must, within 14 days after the date of the order, notify the parties to the hearing and any representatives of the parties in writing of—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the making of the order;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the effective date of the order;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the reasons for making the order; and

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: if it is an order made under subsection (3)(b)—the period during which the ordered removal has effect.

subsection.content: Subject to subsection (2), a disciplinary board making a decision under section 48(3) (first decision) must, after the expiry of the specified period, order the first decision be published in the Gazette, or in any other way the board considers appropriate, if no notice of appeal is given during that period.

subsection.leadIn: If the first decision is appealed against in an appeal board, the disciplinary board must—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: within 30 days after the appeal board has made its decision, order the decision of the appeal board be published in the Gazette, or in any other way the disciplinary board considers appropriate; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: where the appeal is withdrawn or abandoned, within 30 days after the withdrawal or abandonment, order the first decision be published in the Gazette, or in any other way the disciplinary board considers appropriate.

subsection.content: An order made under subsection (1) or (2) may include any particulars the disciplinary board considers appropriate for members of the public to know about the nature of the matter to which the first decision or the decision of the appeal board relates.
For the purposes of the law of defamation, a person does not incur any civil liability by reason only of publishing an order or other particulars permitted under this section.

subsection.leadIn: In this section—
subsection.def: specified period (指明期間), in relation to a registered fire engineer to whom a first decision relates, means a 30-day period beginning on the date immediately following the date on which the registered fire engineer is notified of the decision.

section.name: s50
section.heading: Privileges and immunities of members of disciplinary board etc.

subsection.content: Members of a disciplinary board have, in performing their functions under this Part, the same privileges and immunities as a judge of the Court of First Instance in civil proceedings in that Court.

A person who appears before a disciplinary board (including a party to the complaint concerned, the party’s representative and a witness) and the board’s legal adviser are entitled to the same privileges and immunities as the person and the legal adviser respectively would have in civil proceedings in the Court of First Instance.

def.name: OriginalDecision
def.leadIn: original decision (原有決定), in relation to an appeal made under section 52(1), means—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a decision of the Director to refuse an application for registration under section 9(1)(b);

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a decision of the Director to refuse an application for renewal of registration under section 11(3)(b);

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: a decision of the Director to remove the name of a registered fire engineer from the register as described in section 15(4); or

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: a decision of the Director to refuse to refer a complaint to the Secretary under section 39(4);

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: in relation to an appeal made under section 52(1)—an order made by a disciplinary board under section 48(3); or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: in relation to an appeal made under section 52(3)—an order made by a disciplinary board under section 48(2) or (3);

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.leadIn: in relation to an appeal made under section 52(1)—

subparagraph.content: the Director; or
the person making the appeal; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: in relation to an appeal made under section 52(3)—

subparagraph.content: the Director; or
the disciplinary board the order of which is appealed against.

subsection.content: If a person (other than the Director) is aggrieved by an original decision or original order made in relation to the person, the person may appeal to an appeal board against the decision or order in accordance with this Part.

Unless the Director or disciplinary board concerned decides otherwise, an appeal made under subsection (1) does not suspend the original decision or original order (as appropriate) that is the subject of the appeal.
If the Director is aggrieved by an original order, the Director may appeal to an appeal board against the order in accordance with this Part.
Unless the disciplinary board concerned decides otherwise, an appeal made under subsection (3) does not suspend the order that is the subject of the appeal.
A decision of an appeal board is final.

section.name: s53
section.heading: Commencement of appeal by persons other than Director

subsection.content: If a person (other than the Director) intends to appeal under section 52(1), the person must commence the appeal by giving the Director a notice of appeal in the specified form.

subsection.leadIn: The notice of appeal must be given to the Director within—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a 30-day period beginning on the date immediately following the date on which the person was notified of the original decision or original order (as appropriate) appealed against; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a longer period the Secretary allows.

subsection.leadIn: The notice of appeal—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must set out the grounds of the appeal and the facts relied on;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be accompanied by a copy of every document that the person intends to rely on; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: must include particulars of every witness whom the person intends to call at the hearing.

subsection.content: On receiving a notice of appeal that complies with subsection (3), the Director must deliver the notice to the Secretary within a 14-day period beginning on the date immediately following the date of receipt.

subsection.leadIn: If the Director intends to appeal under section 52(3), the Director must commence the appeal by delivering to the Secretary a notice of appeal in the specified form within—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a 30-day period beginning on the date immediately following the date on which the Director was notified of the original order appealed against; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a longer period the Secretary allows.

subsection.leadIn: The notice of appeal—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must set out the grounds of the appeal and the facts relied on;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be accompanied by a copy of every document that the Director intends to rely on; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: must include particulars of every witness whom the Director intends to call at the hearing.

section.name: s55
section.heading: Appointment of appeal board
section.content: If a notice of appeal is delivered to the Secretary under section 53 or 54, the Secretary must, within 21 days after receiving the notice, appoint a board to hear and consider the appeal.

subsection.leadIn: For hearing an appeal made under section 52 by an appeal board, the chairperson of the board is to—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: appoint the time and place of the hearing; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: notify the parties in writing of that time and place.

subsection.leadIn: A party to the hearing may—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: make a representation in person at the hearing; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: be represented at the hearing by a solicitor or counsel, or any other person authorized by the party in writing.

subsection.content: A party to the hearing and the party’s representative (if any) may adduce evidence at any proceedings before the appeal board.
The hearing is to be open to the public unless the appeal board determines that there is a good reason for it to be held in camera.

section.name: s57
section.heading: Giving of evidence and related offence

subsection.leadIn: For hearing an appeal made under section 52, the appeal board may—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: receive evidence on oath; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: by notice signed by the chairperson of the board, order any person—

subparagraph.content: to attend before the board and to give evidence; or
to produce any document or information relevant to the appeal.

subsection.content: A person who, without reasonable excuse, contravenes an order made under subsection (1)(b) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine at level 5.

If a registered fire engineer is alleged to have committed a disciplinary offence at a time when a code of practice was in force, subsection (2) has effect with respect to the code in relation to the alleged offence.

The appeal board may, in any proceedings under this Regulation to decide whether a registered fire engineer has committed a disciplinary offence, have regard to any provision of the code that appears to the board to be relevant to the act or omission constituting the offence.

section.name: s59
section.heading: Legal adviser to appeal board
section.content: The chairperson of an appeal board may appoint a solicitor or counsel as a legal adviser to advise on any legal matters relating to the proceedings of the board.

section.name: s60
section.heading: Orders by appeal board after hearing

subsection.content: After hearing an appeal made under section 52, the appeal board may make an order to confirm, revoke or vary, or substitute the board’s own decision for, the original decision or original order concerned.

If the appeal board decides to revoke or vary the original decision or original order, or to substitute the board’s own decision for the original decision or original order, the board may order the Director or the disciplinary board concerned (as the case requires) to take any appropriate action to give effect to the appeal board’s decision.

subsection.leadIn: If the appeal board makes a decision under subsection (1), the board must, within 14 days after the date of the decision, notify the parties to the hearing and any representatives of the parties in writing of—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the making of the decision, including any order made under subsection (2);

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the reasons for making the decision; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: in relation to an order made under subsection (2)—the details of the order.

section.name: s61
section.heading: Privileges and immunities of members of appeal board etc.

subsection.content: Members of an appeal board have, in performing their functions under this Division, the same privileges and immunities as a judge of the Court of First Instance in civil proceedings in that Court.

A person who appears before an appeal board (including a party to the appeal concerned, the party’s representative and a witness) and the board’s legal adviser are entitled to the same privileges and immunities as the person and the legal adviser respectively would have in civil proceedings in the Court of First Instance.

part.name: P8
part.heading: Registration Committee, Board Panels and Boards

subsection.content: The Director must establish a fire engineers registration committee to perform the function under section 63.

subsection.leadIn: The registration committee is to consist of the following members—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a chairperson;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a secretary;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: 10 other members.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the registration committee is to be appointed by the Director in accordance with the following categories—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the chairperson and secretary must be fire services members;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: 1 of the other members of the committee must be a fire services member;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: 4 of the other members of the committee must be nominated by the Engineers Registration Board established under section 3 of the Engineers Registration Ordinance; and

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: 5 of the other members of the committee must be nominated by other relevant professional or academic bodies as the Director considers appropriate.

section.name: s63
section.heading: Function of registration committee
section.content: The function of the registration committee is to advise the Director on the registration of fire engineers, the policy, and on assessment criteria in registering a person as a registered fire engineer for the purposes of this Regulation.

section.name: s64
section.heading: Term of members of registration committee

subsection.content: A member of the registration committee is to be appointed for a term of not more than 3 years and may be reappointed after the expiry of a term.
A member of the registration committee may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Director.
The Director may terminate the appointment of a member of the registration committee if satisfied that a specified event has happened in relation to the member.

section.name: s65
section.heading: Procedure of registration committee
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, the registration committee may regulate its procedure and make standing order for that purpose.

subsection.content: The Director must establish a panel from which the Director is to appoint members to an interview board.
An interview board panel is to consist of at least 3 members.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the interview board panel—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must not be a public officer; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be nominated by relevant professional or academic bodies as the Director considers appropriate, and appointed by the Director.

section.name: s67
section.heading: Term of members of interview board panel

subsection.content: A member of the interview board panel is to be appointed for a term of not more than 3 years and may be reappointed after the expiry of a term.
A member of the interview board panel may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Director.

subsection.leadIn: The Director may terminate the appointment of a member of the interview board panel if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the member becomes a public officer; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the Director is satisfied that a specified event has happened in relation to the member.

section.name: s68
section.heading: Procedure of interview board panel
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, the interview board panel may regulate its procedure and may make standing order for that purpose.

subsection.leadIn: An interview board is to consist of—

subparagraph.content: a chairperson;
2 other members; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a secretary to the board.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the interview board is to be appointed by the Director in accordance with the following categories—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the chairperson must be a fire services member;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: 1 of the members must be a fire services member; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: 1 of the other members must be appointed from the interview board panel.

subsection.content: If, in the course of performing the functions of an interview board, a member of the interview board concerned ceases to be a member of the interview board panel (other than for the reason under section 67(3)), the member may continue to take part in performing those functions.
The secretary to an interview board is to provide administrative services to the board.

subsection.leadIn: The secretary to an interview board—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: is to be appointed by the Director; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be a fire services member.

subsection.content: The Director may not appoint the same fire services member to be both a member of and a secretary to an interview board.
The Director may appoint one or more interview boards at any one time.

section.name: s70
section.heading: Functions of interview board
section.leadIn: The functions of an interview board are as follows—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: to examine the qualifications of an applicant for registration as a registered fire engineer;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: to conduct a professional interview with such an applicant;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: to inquire such an applicant to ascertain the applicant’s relevant experience;

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: to advise the Director whether to approve or refuse an application.

subsection.content: An interview board is to meet as often as the chairperson of the board directs.
An interview board may determine its own procedure.

section.name: s72
section.heading: Disclosure of interests of member of interview board
section.leadIn: If a member of an interview board becomes aware that the member has a pecuniary or personal interest, whether direct or indirect, in an applicant for registration as a registered fire engineer, the member— (L.N. 207 of 2025)

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must, before or as soon as practicable after the interview concerned begins, disclose to the board the fact and the nature of the interest;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must withdraw from the interview if so required by the board; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: must not participate in any deliberation regarding the interview.

subsection.content: The Secretary must establish a panel from which the Secretary is to appoint members to a disciplinary board.
A disciplinary board panel is to consist of at least 3 members.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the disciplinary board panel—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must not be a public officer; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be nominated by relevant professional or academic bodies as the Secretary considers appropriate, and appointed by the Secretary.

section.name: s74
section.heading: Term of members of disciplinary board panel

subsection.content: A member of the disciplinary board panel is to be appointed for a term of not more than 3 years and may be reappointed after the expiry of a term.
A member of the disciplinary board panel may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Secretary.

subsection.leadIn: The Secretary may terminate the appointment of a member of the disciplinary board panel if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the member becomes a public officer; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the Secretary is satisfied that a specified event has happened in relation to the member.

section.name: s75
section.heading: Procedure of disciplinary board panel
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, the disciplinary board panel may regulate its procedure and make standing order for that purpose.

subsection.content: A disciplinary board is to consist of 5 members and a secretary to the board.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the disciplinary board is to be appointed by the Secretary in accordance with the following categories—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: 2 of the members must be fire services members; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: 3 of the other members must be appointed from the disciplinary board panel.

subsection.content: If a fire services member is or was engaged, whether directly or indirectly, in the investigation of a complaint to be considered by the disciplinary board, the Secretary may not appoint that fire services member to be a member of the board.

If, in the course of considering a complaint, a member of the disciplinary board concerned ceases to be a member of the disciplinary board panel (other than for the reason under section 74(3)), the member may continue to consider the complaint until a decision is made by the board in respect of the complaint.
The secretary to a disciplinary board is to provide administrative services to the board.

subsection.leadIn: The secretary to a disciplinary board—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: is to be appointed by the Secretary; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be a fire services member.

subsection.content: The Secretary may not appoint the same fire services member to be both a member of and a secretary to a disciplinary board.
The Secretary may appoint one or more disciplinary boards at any one time.
Members of a disciplinary board are to elect the chairperson of the board from among themselves.
The chairperson is to preside at any meeting of the disciplinary board.
All questions for decision are to be decided by a majority of votes of the board members present and voting.
If there is an equality of votes, the chairperson has a casting vote as well as a deliberative vote.
The quorum of a meeting of a disciplinary board is 4 board members.

If a board member is disqualified from taking part in a decision or deliberation in respect of a matter under section 79, the member must be disregarded for constituting the quorum for deciding or deliberating on that matter.

section.name: s79
section.heading: Disclosure of interests of member of disciplinary board
section.leadIn: If a member of a disciplinary board becomes aware that the member has a pecuniary or personal interest, whether direct or indirect, in any matter under consideration at a meeting of the disciplinary board, the member— (L.N. 207 of 2025)

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must, before or as soon as practicable after the meeting begins, disclose to the board the fact and the nature of the interest;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must withdraw from the meeting while the board is considering the matter if so required by the board; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: must not participate in any deliberation or be involved in any decision regarding the matter.

section.name: s80
section.heading: Procedure of disciplinary board
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, a disciplinary board may determine its own procedure.

subsection.content: The Secretary must establish a panel from which the Secretary is to appoint members to an appeal board.
An appeal board panel is to consist of at least 5 members.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the appeal board panel—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must not be a public officer; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be nominated by relevant professional or academic bodies as the Secretary considers appropriate, and appointed by the Secretary.

section.name: s82
section.heading: Term of members of appeal board panel

subsection.content: A member of the appeal board panel is to be appointed for a term of not more than 3 years and may be reappointed after the expiry of a term.
A member of the appeal board panel may resign at any time by giving written notice to the Secretary.

subsection.leadIn: The Secretary may terminate the appointment of a member of the appeal board panel if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the member becomes a public officer; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the Secretary is satisfied that a specified event has happened in relation to the member.

section.name: s83
section.heading: Procedure of appeal board panel
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, the appeal board panel may regulate its procedure and make standing order for that purpose.

subsection.content: An appeal board is to consist of 7 members and a secretary to the board.

subsection.leadIn: Each member of the appeal board is to be appointed by the Secretary in accordance with the following categories—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: 2 of the members must be fire services members; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: 5 of the other members must be appointed from the appeal board panel.

subsection.content: If a fire services member or member of the appeal board panel was engaged, whether directly or indirectly, in the making of an original decision (as defined by section 51) that is the subject of an appeal to be considered by the appeal board, the Secretary may not appoint that fire services member or panel member to be a member of the appeal board.

If a fire services member or member of the appeal board panel was a member of a disciplinary board the order of which is the subject of an appeal to be considered by the appeal board, the Secretary may not appoint that fire services member or panel member to be a member of the appeal board.

If a fire services member is or was engaged, whether directly or indirectly, in the investigation of a complaint that is the subject of a decision or an order appealed against under section 52, the Secretary may not appoint that fire services member to be a member of the appeal board that considers the decision or order.

If, in the course of considering an appeal, a member of the appeal board concerned ceases to be a member of the appeal board panel (other than for the reason under section 82(3)), the member may continue to consider the appeal until a decision is made by the board in respect of the appeal.
The secretary to an appeal board is to provide administrative services to the board.

subsection.leadIn: The secretary to an appeal board—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: is to be appointed by the Secretary; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must be a fire services member.

subsection.content: The Secretary may not appoint the same fire services member to be both a member of and a secretary to an appeal board.
The Secretary may appoint one or more appeal boards at any one time.
Members of an appeal board are to elect the chairperson of the board from among themselves.
The chairperson is to preside at any meeting of the appeal board.
All questions for decision are to be decided by a majority of votes of the board members present and voting.
If there is an equality of votes, the chairperson has a casting vote as well as a deliberative vote.
The quorum of a meeting of an appeal board is 5 board members.

If a board member is disqualified from taking part in a decision or deliberation in respect of a matter under section 87, the member must be disregarded for constituting the quorum for deciding or deliberating on that matter.

section.name: s87
section.heading: Disclosure of interests of member of appeal board
section.leadIn: If a member of an appeal board becomes aware that the member has a pecuniary or personal interest, whether direct or indirect, in any matter under consideration at a meeting of the appeal board, the member— (L.N. 207 of 2025)

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must, before or as soon as practicable after the meeting begins, disclose to the board the fact and the nature of the interest;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must withdraw from the meeting while the board is considering the matter if so required by the board; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: must not participate in any deliberation or be involved in any determination regarding the matter.

section.name: s88
section.heading: Procedure of appeal board
section.content: Except as provided in this Regulation, an appeal board may determine its own procedure.

section.name: s89
section.heading: Director to issue code of practice

subsection.leadIn: The Director may issue a code of practice that in the Director’s opinion is suitable for—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: providing practical guidance on any matter concerning the professional conduct, administration and registration of registered fire engineers; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: providing practical guidance on any matter concerning the fire safety of any scheduled premises, including—

subparagraph.content: providing practical guidance to a registered fire engineer (risk assessment) on assessing fire risk of the scheduled premises and issuing the fire safety requirement; and

providing practical guidance to a registered fire engineer (fire service installation) or registered fire engineer (ventilating system) on the duties imposed by sections 28(1) or 29(1) (as the case may be).

subsection.leadIn: If a code of practice is issued under subsection (1), the Director must by notice published in the Gazette—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: identify the code; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: specify the date on which the code is to take effect.

subsection.content: The Director may from time to time revise or revoke a code of practice issued under subsection (1).

subsection.leadIn: If a code of practice is revised or revoked under subsection (3), the Director must by notice published in the Gazette—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: identify the revision or revocation;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: specify the date on which the revision or revocation is to take effect; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: specify the purposes for which the code is revised or revoked.

subsection.content: A failure by a registered fire engineer to observe a code of practice does not of itself make the engineer liable to any civil or criminal proceedings.

subsection.leadIn: Despite subsection (5), if in any legal proceedings the court is satisfied that a code of practice is relevant to determining a matter that is in issue in the proceedings—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the code is admissible in evidence in the proceedings; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: proof that the person contravened or did not contravene a relevant provision of the code may be relied on by a party to the proceedings as tending to establish or negate that matter.

subsection.content: A code of practice issued under this section is not subsidiary legislation.

subsection.leadIn: In this section—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a court as defined by section 3 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 1);

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: a magistrate as defined by section 3 of the Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 1);

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: a disciplinary board; or

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: an appeal board;

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the proceedings of a disciplinary board; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the proceedings of an appeal board.

subsection.content: The Director may specify the form of a document required for the purposes of this Regulation.
The Director may specify more than one form of the document, whether as alternatives or to provide for different circumstances.

subsection.leadIn: A form specified under this section—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: must be completed in accordance with the directions and instructions that are specified in the form; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: if the completed form is required to be provided to the Director or any other person, must be so provided in the way specified in the form.

subsection.content: A form specified under this section is not subsidiary legislation.

section.name: s91
section.heading: Director to establish and keep register

subsection.content: The Director must, for the purposes of this Regulation, establish and keep a register of registered fire engineers.

subsection.leadIn: The register must contain the following information of each of the registered fire engineers—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the name;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the registration number;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the class for which the engineer is registered; and

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: the expiry date of the registration.

subsection.content: The register may be kept in a form, and may contain any other information, that the Director considers appropriate.
The register must be made available to any person who wishes to ascertain whether a person is a registered fire engineer.

subsection.leadIn: The register—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: is to be published in the Gazette at least once in every year; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: is to be published from time to time, and in a way, as the Director considers appropriate.

subsection.content: The Director may, in writing, appoint a public officer to be an authorized officer.
The Director may perform any duty, or exercise any power, of an authorized officer under this Regulation.

section.name: s93
section.heading: Delegation of Director’s duties or powers

subsection.content: The Director may, in writing, delegate to a public officer any of the Director’s duties or powers under this Regulation.
However, the power to delegate conferred by subsection (1) may not be delegated.

section.name: s94
section.heading: Performance of duties and exercise of powers
section.leadIn: When performing a duty or exercising a power under this Regulation, a public officer to whom such a duty or power is delegated under section 93(1) or an authorized officer—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: may be assisted by any person whom the officer reasonably requires; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: must produce proof of the officer’s identity for inspection by a person who is affected by the performance of the duty or the exercise of the power and requires to see it.

section.name: s95
section.heading: Service of notices or other documents

subsection.leadIn: A notice or other document (however described) required to be given or sent under this Regulation is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, served if—

subparagraph.content: it is addressed to the Director and delivered to the Director’s principal office;
it is sent to the Director by post addressed to the address specified by the Director;
it is sent to the Director by fax transmission addressed to the Director at the fax number specified by the Director; or

subparagraph.leadIn: it is sent in the form of an electronic record to the Director—

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: by an electronic mail transmission addressed to the Director at the electronic mail address specified by the Director; or

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: through an information system specified by the Director;
it is addressed to and delivered personally to the person;
it is sent to the person by post addressed to the person at the person’s last known address;
it is sent to the person by fax transmission addressed to the person at the person’s last known fax number; or

subparagraph.leadIn: it is sent in the form of an electronic record to the person—

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: by an electronic mail transmission addressed to the person at the person’s last known electronic mail address; or

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: through an information system specified by the Director;

it is addressed to the partnership and delivered to a place in Hong Kong at which the partnership carries on business, and given to a person apparently concerned in the management of, or apparently employed by, the partnership;
it is sent to the partnership by post addressed to the partnership at the partnership’s last known address;
it is sent to the partnership by fax transmission addressed to the partnership at the partnership’s last known fax number; or

subparagraph.leadIn: it is sent in the form of an electronic record to the partnership—

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: by an electronic mail transmission addressed to the partnership at the partnership’s last known electronic mail address; or

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: through an information system specified by the Director;
it is addressed to the company and delivered to any officer of the company;
it is left at, or sent by post to, the company’s registered office within the meaning of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622);
it is sent to the company by post addressed to the company at the company’s last known address;
it is sent to the company by fax transmission addressed to the company at the company’s last known fax number; or

subparagraph.leadIn: it is sent in the form of an electronic record to the company—

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: by an electronic mail transmission addressed to the company at the company’s last known electronic mail address; or

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: through an information system specified by the Director; or

it is addressed to the body and delivered to a place in Hong Kong at which the body carries on business, and given to a person apparently concerned in the management of, or apparently employed by, the body;
it is sent to the body by post addressed to the body at the body’s last known address;
it is sent to the body by fax transmission addressed to the body at the body’s last known fax number; or

subparagraph.leadIn: it is sent in the form of an electronic record to the body—

subparagraph.name: A
subparagraph.content: by an electronic mail transmission addressed to the body at the body’s last known electronic mail address; or

subparagraph.name: B
subparagraph.content: through an information system specified by the Director.

subsection.leadIn: A notice or document given or sent in accordance with subsection (1) is taken to have been served on the addressee—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: if delivered personally—on the day of delivery;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: if sent by post—at the time at which the notice or document would be delivered in the ordinary course of post;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: if sent by fax transmission—on the day after the day on which it was sent; or

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: if sent in the form of an electronic record—on the day after the day on which it was sent.

subsection.content: An electronic record sent under this section must be signed by the sender.

subsection.leadIn: The requirement for a signature on the electronic record under subsection (3) is met by—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.leadIn: if the sender is a natural person—

subparagraph.content: a digital signature of the person; or
a password of that person assigned or approved under subsection (5); and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.leadIn: if the sender is not a natural person—

subparagraph.content: a digital signature of a natural person who is authorized by the sender to send the electronic record for that sender; or
a password of the sender assigned or approved under subsection (5).

subsection.content: The Director may, for enabling a person to send an electronic record under this section, assign or approve any sequence or combination of letters, characters, numbers or symbols of any language as the person’s password.

A person whose digital signature has been affixed on the electronic record under subsection (4)(b)(i) is, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, to be regarded as a person who is authorized by the sender to send the record for the sender.

subsection.leadIn: In this section—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a body corporate other than a company; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: an unincorporated body of persons other than a partnership;

subsection.def: company (公司) has the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622);
digital signature (數碼簽署) means a digital signature within the meaning of section 2(1) of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance that meets the requirements specified in section 96;

def.name: ElectronicMailAddress
def.leadIn: electronic mail address (電郵地址) includes—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: a number; or

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: any sequence or combination of letters, characters, numbers or symbols of any language,

def.continued: used for sending or receiving a document in electronic form;

subsection.def: electronic record (電子紀錄) has the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance.

section.name: s96
section.heading: Requirements specified for digital signature under section 95(7)

subsection.leadIn: The requirements specified for the definition of digital signature in section 95(7) are that—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: the digital signature is supported by a recognized certificate;

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the digital signature is generated within the validity of the certificate; and

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: the digital signature is used in accordance with the terms of that certificate.

subsection.leadIn: In this section—
subsection.def: certification authority (核證機關) has the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance;
recognized certificate (認可證書) has the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance;
recognized certification authority (認可核證機關) has the meaning given by section 2(1) of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance;

def.name: WithinTheValidityOfTheCertificate
def.leadIn: within the validity of the certificate (在該證書的有效期內) means that at the time the digital signature is generated—

paragraph.name: a
b
paragraph.content: the recognition of the certificate has not been revoked or suspended by the Commissioner for Digital Policy;

paragraph.name: c
paragraph.content: if it is a certificate designated as a recognized certificate issued by the recognized certification authority referred to in section 34 of the Electronic Transactions Ordinance—the designation has not been withdrawn by the certification authority;

paragraph.name: d
paragraph.content: if the Commissioner for Digital Policy has specified a period of validity for the recognition of the certificate—the certificate is within that period; and

paragraph.name: e
paragraph.content: if the recognized certification authority has specified a period of validity for the certificate—the certificate is within that period.

section.name: s97
section.heading: Electronic and hard copy forms of registration card

subsection.content: Subject to subsection (2), a registration card must be in an electronic form specified by the Director.

The Director may issue a registration card in a hard copy form specified by the Director to a registered fire engineer if the engineer has shown sufficient ground to the satisfaction of the Director that the card should be issued in such a form.

section.name: s98
section.heading: Fees paid not refundable
section.content: Any fee paid under this Regulation is not refundable.

subsection.content: This section applies if a provision of this Regulation that creates an offence makes a reference to a reasonable excuse for a contravention or failure to which the provision relates.
The reference to a reasonable excuse is to be construed as providing for a defence to a charge in respect of the contravention or failure to which the provision relates.

subsection.leadIn: A defendant is taken to have established that the defendant had a reasonable excuse for the contravention or failure if—

paragraph.name: a
paragraph.content: there is sufficient evidence to raise an issue that the defendant had such a reasonable excuse; and

paragraph.name: b
paragraph.content: the contrary is not proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
